request.statement:
Build a migration reporter for a versioned diagnostic-category catalog.

A catalog entry is identified by `(provider, resource, symbol)` and stores one case-sensitive wire value. Catalog versions form a tree: version `0` is empty, and each version `i` derives from one earlier version.

Write one complete Rust program containing `fn main()`. Use only the standard library.

Input begins with `V Q`, where `1 <= V,Q <= 120000`.

The next `V` lines define versions `1..V`. Each begins with its parent `p`, where `0 <= p < i`, followed by one operation:

- `SET provider resource symbol wire`: create or replace the entry.
- `DELETE provider resource symbol`: remove the entry, doing nothing if absent.
- `MOVE sp sr ss dp dr ds`: if the source entry is absent, do nothing. Otherwise atomically remove it and store its wire at the destination, replacing any destination entry. If source and destination keys are identical, nothing changes.
- `CLONE sp sr dp dr`: atomically replace the entire destination provider/resource scope with an exact copy of the source scope from the parent catalog. Thus destination entries whose symbols are absent from the source are removed. The source is unchanged. If both scopes are identical, nothing changes.

Every operation reads only the parent catalog; siblings never affect one another.

The next `Q` lines contain `old new provider resource`, requesting a report between versions `old` and `new`, each in `0..V`, for exactly that scope.

For every symbol present in either scoped catalog, output one of:

- `ADDED symbol newWire` if present only in `new`.
- `REMOVED symbol oldWire` if present only in `old`.
- `UNCHANGED symbol wire` if both wire values are identical.
- `CHANGED symbol oldWire newWire` otherwise.

For each query, first print its record count, then print its records in ascending lexicographic order of `symbol`. Reports follow consecutively without separators.

All names and wire values are nonempty ASCII strings using bytes 33 through 126 and contain no whitespace. Comparisons are case-sensitive; lexicographic order compares unsigned ASCII bytes. Wire values need not be unique.

Across all operations and queries, the sum of the numbers of distinct provider/resource pairs and distinct symbol strings is at most `400000`. Across all queries, at most `250000` records are printed.

Standard input contains the format above. Write the reports to standard output. Output is judged by splitting only on ASCII whitespace bytes `0x09` through `0x0D` and `0x20`, then comparing tokens exactly in order and count.
